title: The pairing is the duality isomorphism
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $a,n\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] for these parameters, with its bounded constructible finite-Tor categories and coefficient conventions. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $X$ be a smooth separated finite-type geometrically connected $k$-scheme of pure dimension $d\geq0$, and let $a_X:X\to s$ be its structure morphism. Assume either that $X$ is proper, or that $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth separated finite-type geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$; no properness is required in the latter case. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$, put $K^\vee=R\mathcal H om_X(K,\Lambda_X)$, and fix an orientation [def-sf-orientation] for $a_X$. Use the Verdier dual $\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal H om_X(K,Ra_X^!\Lambda_s)$ of [def-sf-pf] and the global-duality map of [thm-sf-global-duality]. Let $\beta_K$ denote the derived pairing of [def-sf-pairing], the mixed-support cup product of [def-sf-cup] followed by twisted evaluation and the normalized smooth trace (the counit through the fixed orientation):
$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
\xrightarrow{\smile_c}R\Gamma_c(X,K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee(d))[2d]
\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(\operatorname{ev}_K(d))[2d]}R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d))[2d]
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}}\Lambda.
$$
Here $R\Gamma$ and $R\Gamma_c$ are the ordinary and compact-support point-category images, or their coefficient complexes via [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], respectively. A pairing $C\otimes^L_\Lambda D\to\Lambda$ is called perfect when its tensor--internal-Hom adjoint $D\to R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)$ is an isomorphism, as in [def-sf-pairing]. Then the tensor–internal-Hom adjoint of
$\beta_K$ is the canonical isomorphism

$$
b_K^\sharp:\ R\Gamma\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda\bigl(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda\bigr)
$$

in the point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, and its inverse is the global
duality isomorphism of [thm-sf-global-duality] followed by the
identification $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ induced by the orientation.
In particular $\beta_K$ is perfect. If $X$ is proper and
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, its degreewise form
gives perfect pairings

$$
\langle-,-\rangle_i:H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)
\longrightarrow\Lambda\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z),
$$

the line-valued form being $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\to \Lambda(-d)$.
For nonproper $X$ the degreewise assertion over field coefficients is
recorded separately in the Poincare duality chapter
(thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field).

proof.text: Construct the canonical isomorphism, keeping its direction explicit. Work first in the point category, writing $F=Ra_{X!}$, $G=Ra_X^!$, $U=La_X^*$, $P=Ra_{X*}$, $1=\Lambda_s$, $C=FK$, $\omega=G1$, and $H=R\mathcal H om_X(K,\omega)=\mathbb D_XK$, with the notation of [def-sf-pf]. Put $L=K^\vee(d)[2d]$ and $V=PL=R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$, using the derived shift comparisons. Perfectness of $K$ implies perfectness of $K^\vee$ by [prop-sf-dualizable], so the pairing in [def-sf-pairing] is defined. Write $\gamma:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega$ for [def-sf-orientation]. The canonical evaluation comparison of [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] at $M=\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ (the inverse of the twist-interchange identification of [lem-sf-twist-interchange]), followed by $R\mathcal H om_X(K,\gamma)$, gives $\theta:L\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. By [thm-sf-global-duality] there is a canonical $g:C^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}PH$ when $X$ is proper or $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ with the smooth separated finite-type geometrically connected $X_0$ specified above. Here $g$ means the point-category transport specified in the current statement of [thm-sf-global-duality], not an identification of its four coefficient targets. Its finite-stage exceptional-admissibility bounds are automatic for the separated finite-type structure morphism; its integral and field adjunctions are those of the fixed datum, so no extra hypothesis on $X$ or $K$ is being assumed. Axioms (A1) and (A6) of [def-sf-datum] put $C$, $C^\vee$, $H$ and $PH$ on the finite-Tor domains; $PL$ is isomorphic to $PH$ by $P\theta$ and is on that domain too. In particular the tensor comparisons below apply to these objects. Define $h=g^{-1}\circ P\theta:V\xrightarrow{\sim}C^\vee$. Its inverse is $(P\theta)^{-1}\circ g$, exactly global duality followed by the oriented identification in the statement. Here and below the notation $R\Gamma$ in a point-category formula means $Ra_{X*}$; applying the coefficient evaluation of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] gives the module-complex notation. The exact point equivalence in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] is compatible with tensor and its unit by [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. It therefore also preserves the closed dual and its evaluation: for a finite-Tor point object $T$, the natural bijections are $\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Fib}_sT,\operatorname{Fib}_s(C^\vee))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,C^\vee)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(C\otimes^LT,1)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Fib}_sC\otimes^L\operatorname{Fib}_sT,\Lambda)$. Here both arguments of each $\operatorname{Hom}_s$ lie in the point category, and both arguments of each un-subscripted $\operatorname{Hom}$ lie in its coefficient-complex target. Taking T to be the representing objects in both directions shows that this identification and its inverse are inverse, and taking the identity gives preservation of evaluation. Thus the calculation in the point category transports to the stated coefficient-complex pairing, including its adjoint. Write $\alpha_C:\operatorname{Fib}_s(C^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(\operatorname{Fib}_sC,\Lambda)$ for this evaluation-preserving comparison. If $g_{\mathrm{coeff}}$ denotes the coefficient-complex arrow of [thm-sf-global-duality], its point transport is characterized by $\operatorname{Fib}_s(g)=g_{\mathrm{coeff}}\circ\alpha_C$. This equation fixes both the source comparison and the direction used in $h$.

Compute the adjunction chain on actual morphisms. The adjunctions and projection isomorphism invoked here are precisely axioms (A1), (A3) of [def-sf-datum], with the projection transformation of [def-sf-pf]. For $T$ in the finite-Tor point category and $t:T\to PH$, the chain is
$$\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,PH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(UT,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K\otimes^L UT,G1)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(F(K\otimes^L UT),1)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(C\otimes^L T,1).$$
Let $\epsilon:UP\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\mu:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ be the respective counits, and let $e:K\otimes^LH\to\omega$ be internal-Hom evaluation. The four arrows send $t$, successively, to $\epsilon_H\circ Ut$, to $e\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon_H)\circ(1_K\otimes Ut)$, to $\mu_1\circ F(e\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon_H)\circ(1_K\otimes Ut))$, and finally to
$$\mu_1\circ F(e\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon_H)\circ(1_K\otimes Ut))\circ\operatorname{PF}_{K,T}.$$
This writes out the chain defining the canonical tensor--Hom exchange of [lem-sf-tensor-hom] at $f=a_X,M=K,N=1$. Thus its map $\Phi:PH\xrightarrow{\sim}C^\vee$ is obtained by currying this expression with $T=PH,t=1_{PH}$; [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] supplies the evaluation formula for uncurry. Now compare with the map that [thm-sf-global-duality] specifies. Its statement transports, through the point equivalence, the exchange isomorphism $e_K:D_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}PH$ of [thm-sf-verdier-exchange] at $f=a_X$, $Y=s$, $M=K$, followed by the evaluation-preserving point comparison of duals. Here $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_s)$ with $\omega_s=Ra_s^!1$. The map $e_K$ is the inverse of the tensor--Hom exchange of [lem-sf-tensor-hom] at $N=\omega_s$, followed by $P\,R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)$ for the mate isomorphism $c:Ra_X^!Ra_s^!1\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_X^!1$ of the composition $a_X=a_s\circ a_X$. The structure morphism $a_s=\mathrm{id}_s$ is proper with $Ra_{s!}\cong\mathrm{id}$ by (A4) of [def-sf-datum]. The counit $\varepsilon^s:\omega_s=Ra_{s!}Ra_s^!1\to1$ of $Ra_{s!}\dashv Ra_s^!$ is then the isomorphism $\omega_s\cong1$ of [lem-sf-point] (1). By [lem-sf-mate], the counit of the composite adjunction is the pasted one, $\mu\circ Ra_{X!}(c)=\varepsilon^s\circ Ra_{s!}(\mu^{\omega})$, where $\mu^{\omega}$ is the counit at $\omega_s$. Transposing this equation gives $c=Ra_X^!(\varepsilon^s)$. Naturality of the exchange of [lem-sf-tensor-hom] in $N$, along $\varepsilon^s:\omega_s\to1$, therefore gives $e_K^{-1}=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\varepsilon^s)^{-1}\circ\Phi$. Under the identification $C^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,1)\cong D_sC$ induced by $\varepsilon^s$, which is the dual comparison that global duality uses, this says $\Phi=g^{-1}$ for the canonical $g$ of [thm-sf-global-duality]. No comparison between $F$ and $P$ is used. With the notation of Step 1 this says $g_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\Phi^{-1})\circ\alpha_C^{-1}$: the inverse Hom chain is evaluated in the coefficient category only after the evaluation-preserving dual comparison. Thus the revised coefficient-first formulation of global duality gives the same $g$, and not a second choice of an isomorphism between its objects.

source.place: Step 2: tensor--Hom chain, with every transpose written out

proof.text:
Identify the pairing, as a morphism rather than just on cohomology. By [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] and Step 2,
$$\operatorname{uncurry}(h)=\mu_1\circ F\bigl(e\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon_H)\bigr)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{K,PH}\circ(1_C\otimes P\theta).$$
Naturality gives the two typed identities $\operatorname{PF}_{K,PH}\circ(1_C\otimes P\theta)=F(1_K\otimes UP\theta)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{K,PL}$ and $\epsilon_H\circ UP\theta=\theta\circ\epsilon_L$. Substituting these identities changes the right side to
$$\mu_1\circ F\bigl(e\circ(1_K\otimes\theta)\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon_L)\bigr)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{K,PL}.$$
The evaluation comparison of [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] used to define $\theta$ in Step 1 is the transpose of twisted evaluation; uncurrying it, as in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], gives $e\circ(1_K\otimes\theta)=\gamma\circ\operatorname{ev}_K(d)[2d]$: before the shift this is the defining transpose identity for the canonical twist-interchange map of [lem-sf-twist-interchange]. All shift comparisons are the derived ones and the tensor factors retain the order $K$, then its dual, so no interchange sign is introduced. By [def-sf-cup], $F(1_K\otimes\epsilon_L)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{K,PL}$ is the mixed-support cup product. By [def-sf-pairing] and [def-sf-orientation], the remaining $\mu_1\circ F\gamma$ is the normalized trace. Consequently this expression is exactly $\beta_K$. Applying the inverse of the tensor--Hom adjunction gives $\operatorname{curry}(\beta_K)=h$; the inverse identities in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] justify cancellation. Since $h$ is an isomorphism by Step 1, $\beta_K$ is perfect in the sense of [def-sf-pairing]. This proves equality of the canonical maps and their specified inverse without the invalid inference that isomorphism detection detects equality.

source.place: Steps 2--3: compute the transpose and cancel the adjunction bijection

proof.text:
For the degreewise assertion impose properness and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], the point category is the bounded finite-cohomology module category at the respective stage, and $C$ is the compact-support coefficient complex. By [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius], $\Lambda$ is self-injective, $\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$ is exact, and finite modules are reflexive under this duality. The complex $\Lambda[0]$ is bounded below and injective termwise, so [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] makes it K-injective. The computation and resolution independence in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], on the one-object ringed site, therefore compute $C^\vee$ by $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_\Lambda(C^\bullet,\Lambda[0])$. Restriction of a degree-$-i$ cocycle to $Z^i(C)$ gives a functional on $H^i(C)$. Every such functional extends from $Z^i(C)/B^i(C)$ to $C^i/B^i(C)$ by injectivity. A cocycle restricting to zero factors through $C^i/Z^i(C)\cong B^{i+1}(C)$, and its functional extends to $C^{i+1}$, so it is a coboundary, up to the invertible sign in the Hom differential. Hence restriction induces a canonical isomorphism
$$H^{-i}(C^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H^i(C),\Lambda).$$
If the chosen tensor--Hom convention writes evaluation in the order $C$ then its dual with a Koszul factor, multiply this restriction comparison by that degree-dependent sign. It is a unit, so the resulting evaluation-induced comparison is still an isomorphism. Use this evaluation-normalized comparison below; it is independent of choices of representatives and involves no splitting of $C$. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it may equivalently be computed at a common finite coefficient field and extended, as in the point-category convention.

source.place: Step 4: exact coefficient duality and its cohomology calculation

proof.text:
Let $D=R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$. Since $\beta_K=\operatorname{uncurry}(h)$, [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] writes it as $\operatorname{ev}_C\circ(1_C\otimes h)$. On representatives, evaluation restricts on a cycle in degree $i$ and a dual cocycle in degree $-i$ to the functional evaluated at that cycle with precisely the Koszul sign of the chosen evaluation convention; boundaries give zero, so the evaluation-normalized restriction calculation of Step 4 identifies the adjoint of the cohomology pairing with $H^{-i}(h)$. The shift convention gives $H^{-i}(D)=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$, and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] gives $H^i(C)=H_c^i(X,K)$. Thus
$$H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H_c^i(X,K),\Lambda).$$
These maps are the degreewise cup/evaluation/trace pairings because Step 3 identifies the underlying derived morphism with the composite of [def-sf-pairing]. Both modules are finite, by the point-category finiteness and the finite-dual clause of [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius]. Dualizing this isomorphism and using the finite-module evaluation isomorphism in that same node gives the adjoint in the other direction, also an isomorphism. This proves perfectness for every integer $i$, including degrees in which both sides vanish.

source.place: Step 4: the adjoint of the degreewise pairing

proof.text:
For the proper line-valued form put $B=\Lambda_s(d)$, the rank-one coefficient line of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Its pullback is $\Lambda_X(d)$: the roots-of-unity formulas pull back from the algebraically closed base, and their compatible finite reductions and scalar extensions give the same assertion at each coefficient stage. By [lem-sf-twist-interchange], $B\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda_s(-d)\cong\Lambda_s$. Since $X$ is proper, (A4) of [def-sf-datum] identifies $F$ and $P$. Applying its projection isomorphism (A3) to $K^\vee$ and $B$ gives
$$R\Gamma(X,K^\vee)\otimes^L_\Lambda B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d)).$$
The line $B$ is free of rank one over the point ring, so tensoring by $B$ is exact; choosing a basis makes the cohomology comparison the identity on the underlying complex, and changing that basis multiplies both sides by the same unit. Therefore canonically $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\otimes_\Lambda B$. The pairing of Step 5, under this identification, is equivalently a pairing $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\to\Lambda(-d)$, by tensoring with the inverse line and contracting $B\otimes B^{-1}$. This is exactly the line-valued form stated. No degreewise assertion over $\mathcal O_E$ or additional assertion for nonproper $X$ is made.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [def-sf-pairing] — so $X$ satisfies the hypotheses of
[thm-sf-global-duality]: $X$ is proper, or $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ with $X_0$
smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected, and no
properness is required in the latter case — suppose in addition that $K$ is
perfect over $\Lambda_X$ and that the orientation of
[def-sf-orientation] is fixed. Then the tensor–internal-Hom adjoint of
$\beta_K$ is the canonical isomorphism

$$
b_K^\sharp:\ R\Gamma\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda\bigl(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda\bigr)
$$

in the point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, and its inverse is the global
duality isomorphism of [thm-sf-global-duality] followed by the
identification $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ induced by the orientation.
In particular $\beta_K$ is perfect. If $X$ is proper and
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, its degreewise form
gives perfect pairings

$$
\langle-,-\rangle_i:H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)
\longrightarrow\Lambda\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z),
$$

the line-valued form being $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\to \Lambda(-d)$.

proof.text:
The cup product, the pairing and the orientation used below are those of
[def-sf-cup], [def-sf-pairing] and [def-sf-orientation],
the projection transformation is [def-sf-pf], and the interchange
law is [lem-sf-twist-interchange].
Steps 1–3 use properness of $X$ nowhere: they use only the global duality
isomorphism of [thm-sf-global-duality], which holds under either of its two
hypotheses, the orientation of [def-sf-orientation] for the smooth
morphism $a_X$, and the formal adjunction calculus of the six-functor
datum; so they prove the derived assertion for proper $X$ and for
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ alike.
Step 1: the two maps. By [thm-sf-global-duality] there is a canonical
isomorphism $R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\to R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$, and by the
orientation $\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal H om_X(K,Ra_X^!\Lambda)\cong R\mathcal H om_X(K,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$; composing gives a
canonical isomorphism
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\to R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$, whose inverse is the map
displayed in the statement. Step 2: the adjoint of the pairing is that
map. The chain of [lem-sf-tensor-hom] with $M=K$, $N=\Lambda$ and
$f=a_X$ is, by [lem-sf-mate] and the definition of the pairing, the
transpose of the composite of cup product, evaluation and trace: taking
$\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,-)$ for $T=\Lambda[-r]$ converts a map $t:T\to R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$ into $b_K^\sharp\circ t$ after the identifications
of [def-sf-pf]. Step 3: conclude by [lem-sf-detection]: the two
maps agree after applying $\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda[-r],-)$ for all $r$,
hence they are equal. Step 4: the degreewise form (for proper $X$) is the
shift convention $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$ together with the identification
$H^{-i}(C^\vee)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H^i(C),\Lambda)$ for a
point complex $C$, applied to $C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$. This identification holds
because $\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$ is exact on
$\Lambda$-modules, so that $R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)$ is
computed termwise and commutes with taking cohomology: for
$\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ this is clear, and
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is self-injective by Baer's
criterion — its ideals are the $\varpi_E^jA_{E,n}$, a homomorphism
$\varphi:\varpi_E^jA_{E,n}\to A_{E,n}$ sends $\varpi_E^j$ to an element
killed by $\varpi_E^{n-j}$, hence to some $\varpi_E^ja$, and
$\varphi$ extends to multiplication by $a$. The adjoint
$H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\to\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H^i_c(X,K),\Lambda)$ of
$\langle-,-\rangle_i$ is then $H^{-i}(b_K^\sharp)$, an isomorphism. (For
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ the degreewise statement is false in general: a
torsion class in $H^i_c(X,K)$ pairs to zero with everything, and
$H^{-i}(C^\vee)$ acquires an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$-contribution from the
torsion of $H^{i+1}(C)$.) The line-valued form is obtained by
eliminating the invertible twist $\Lambda_X(d)$ through
$\Lambda(d)\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(-d)\cong\Lambda$.

split_report.summary: Rebuilt the earlier split in six steps. Expanded the inherited setting into explicit objects, hypotheses and pairing formula after the server B2 check; all conclusions and hypotheses are unchanged. Expanded the tensor--Hom exchange into its actual Hom bijections and counit formula, identified the cup/evaluation/trace morphism by naturality, and used inverse currying to prove equality. Removed the false use of isomorphism detection to infer equality. Computed dual cohomology from a K-injective coefficient ring, proved both degreewise adjoints, and used proper coincidence and projection to remove the Tate twist. All inputs already exist in the DAG; no new nodes. Repair of the returned landing: revalidated the expanded global-duality statement, refreshed its two quotations, and made its coefficient-first versus point-category transport and the finite-Tor domains explicit in Steps 1--2.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes the current blueprint canonical-map paragraph. Steps 2--3 realize the unit tensor--Hom/mate transpose argument; they replace the node-level erroneous cohomology detection inference by an explicit adjunction identity. Steps 4--6 realize the exact-Hom, degreewise, and line-valued clauses of its last paragraph.

tool_uses.why: Only the generic closure of perfect objects under coefficient dual is used to meet the pairing definition; it does not replace the unit tensor--Hom route.
The degreewise step needs self-injectivity, exact ordinary duality and finite-module reflexivity for the three allowed coefficient rings; the unit has no separate coefficient-algebra node.

The generic evaluation comparison for perfect K defines the orientation/twist identification by its transpose and fixes its compatibility with evaluation; this is a tool for the unit pairing calculation.

The exact point equivalence must preserve tensor and evaluation to transport the pairing and its adjoint to coefficient complexes; this generic point-comparison fact does not replace the unit adjunction calculation.
